thread:
maya: Heads-up — PM asked for a console 'marginal-cost playground' that lets SREs/product teams slide routing policies (latency vs cost), toggle prefetch/cache savings, and preview per-model/unit cost delta before rolling policies. Feasibility check + API contract please.
kevin: concrete inputs? do we need per-token effective cost, KV-prefix hit rates, batch-size dist, and per-route latency SLOs?
nate: agree on inputs. big call: telemetry sampling today is 1% for debug traces — not enough for accurate per-model marginal forecasts. we need aggregated counters emitted from router: tokens_by_model_route, cached_prefix_hits_by_model, avg_latency_p50/p95_by_route. coarse granularity (1m) should be fine.
priya: backend sketch: expose a simulate endpoint that accepts a small distribution summary and returns forecast + CI. something like POST /api/v1/simulate/cost with body {model, route, window, seq_len_buckets, cache_hit_override, batch_size_hint}. Could precompute MV for last 24h and compute delta quickly.
ux-lydia: on the UI: slider for routing weight (cost vs latency) + toggles: include prefetch savings, include cache-crediting. show a small uncertainty band (low/med/high) and an "Explain" popover listing top 3 drivers (model size, avg seq len, cache hit). keep it compact on route detail pane.
kevin: realtime compute costs are nontrivial. prefer materialized summary + background job to recompute every 5-15m. realtime on-demand should sample (fast path: estimation using last MV + user overrides). also watch query cost for multi-tenant data access — auth scoping needed.
maya: rollout plan idea: feature-gate to beta orgs, telemetry to compare predicted vs actual next-24h cost (sim_predicted_cost vs observed_burn). add experiment tag so PM can A/B policy changes.
priya: example API payload/response (rough):
```json
POST /api/v1/simulate/cost
{
  "model": "redwood-7b-quant",
  "route": "us-west-1/low-latency",
  "window_minutes": 60,
  "seq_len_buckets": [[0,64,0.6],[65,256,0.3],[257,1024,0.1]],
  "cache_hit_override": 0.12,
  "batch_size_hint": 8
}
```
response 200:
```json
{
  "predicted_cost": 12.45,
  "predicted_tokens": 102345,
  "confidence_interval": [11.1, 14.0],
  "drivers": ["cache_hit_rate","median_seq_len","batch_size"],
  "assumptions": ["uses 5m MV of router counters","extrapolates to 60m"]
}
```
nate: one ops caveat: cardinality — do NOT attach model+route+tenant at 1m resolution into raw TSDB; emit aggregated rollups per model/route and keep tenant-only aggregates coarse. prefer labeled rollups: model, route, env.
ux-lydia: small UX Q: can we add a "simulate impact of routing change" preset that flips allocation to cheaper variant (x%) and shows expected latency and cost deltas? would be handy for on-call folks.
kevin: implementation tasks: 1) router counters + schema, 2) MV job + storage, 3) simulation API + auth, 4) console widget + metrics to measure sim_error. estimate: 2 engineers ~3 sprints if we do MV + UI. lean mode: 1 eng + sampling + simpler widget ~4-6 weeks.
maya: sounds reasonable. @kevin @priya can you own SLO for telemetry + API contract? @ux-lydia can you mock UI for beta? I'll coordinate with PM for beta orgs.
deploy-bot: created task sim-feature/1234 and assigned to kevin/priya. CI pipeline job 4321 queued. :rocket:
priya: one more: for offline validation we should compute sim_error daily per model and surface anomalies (if error > 20% for 3 consecutive days). that'll guard against drift.
nate: yes. and we should store only summary stats for validation (predicted_vs_actual buckets) to avoid cardinality blowup. use 5 coarse seq_len buckets as discussed.
ux-lydia: UX note: default view should show "expected savings" and a quick link "apply to canary" which opens rollout panel prefilled with suggested percentage and evaluation window. keep permission guarded.
maya: awesome — thanks. I'll file the feature spec and link tasks. please drop short PRs for router counter proto and API contract early so infra can review. :thumbsup:
